desc:
AI output quality checks before sending add a safety step between a draft and your customer. Ecom Swift LLC builds a checker that compares each output with your own rules, passes clean items and holds doubtful ones for a person.

## What are quality checks for AI output?

Quality checks are automatic tests applied to a draft before it is sent or published. The checker reads the output and compares it with rules you supplied, such as required wording, banned claims, correct prices and tone notes. Each item gets one of three results: pass, fix or hold, along with a short note explaining what was found.

The checker is a second reader with a very precise checklist. It does not replace your judgment. It makes sure the obvious problems never reach a person's desk or a customer's inbox.

## Why AI drafts need checking

AI tools write confidently, even when they are wrong. A draft can quote a price that does not exist, leave out a required disclaimer, promise a delivery date you cannot meet or drift into a tone that does not fit your brand. These slips are easy to miss when a reviewer reads quickly.

Checking by rule catches the same kind of slip every time, without tiring. It also gives you a record of what kinds of problems appear most often.

## How checks improve results

Customers receive more accurate and consistent messages, which protects trust. Reviewers spend less time hunting for small errors and more time on judgment calls. Because held items come with a note, a reviewer knows where to look first.

The results log shows patterns. If the same rule fails often, the instruction that produces the drafts probably needs improving, and you can fix the cause rather than the symptoms. No checker catches every mistake, so keep a person responsible for sensitive messages.

## What a strong checker includes

- A rule book written in plain words that anyone on your team can read.
- Required phrases, such as a returns line or a legal notice.
- Banned claims and risky wording.
- Facts to compare, such as your price list, policies and opening hours.
- A tone check against samples you provide.
- Three clear results: pass, fix or hold.
- A short note on every problem found.
- A route to a named reviewer for held items.
- A results log so you can see what fails and how often.

## What we do

We collect your rules, your reference facts and a set of past outputs, both good and bad. We turn the rules into a checking step that sits after your drafting tool, whichever tool that is. Small fixes, such as adding a missing line, can be applied automatically. Anything uncertain is held for a person.

We then test the checker on real past outputs and compare its verdicts with your own. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of output types, rules, fact comparisons, tone checks and logging. We finish by writing your rule book so you can edit it later.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Write rules as clear statements that can be answered yes or no.
- Keep your price list and policy facts up to date.
- Include bad examples when you share samples.
- Review held items promptly.
- Add a new rule each time a new kind of mistake appears.

**Avoid:**
- Writing vague rules such as "sound nice".
- Letting the checker approve sensitive messages without a person.
- Changing facts in one place and forgetting the checker.
- Adding so many rules that every item is held.
- Assuming a passed item is perfect.

## Who it is for

A store that sends AI drafted product descriptions can verify that sizes and prices match the catalog. A support team can check that replies always include the correct policy wording. A marketing team can make sure posts avoid claims that are not allowed.

## What we need from you

Send your rules, a few good and bad past outputs and the facts the checker should compare against. Tell us who reviews held items. We never ask for passwords. Access is given as a limited collaborator, team or developer user in the tools involved, and you own everything we build.
